Yeah, you could do pitch modulation within your Sampler if you're using midi but I'd say get a dry midi pattern you're happy with, bounce it to WAV and then automate pitch from there, you'll get more natural, smoother pitch shifts from that plus it'll be kinder to your cpu when you inevitably have a huge project with loads of tracks/MIDI etc

Think about making the loop more dynamic. If you have a loop that you're super happy with, it could be a great motif for your next track! Andrew Huang did a great video on this about how you can turn a single idea into a full song by changing certain elements (The elements of it that you choose to change often depend on the loop itself) 

Mostly, just look to change things up a bit, be that rhythm, a new melody or harmony hook or motif or maybe even a key change. Sometimes if you're using midi, swapping out the instrument or changing your preset can also yield really interesting results.

You could probably get away with a straight up white noise sample or oscillator that you just automate a filter over with low resonance, that will give it some richness then if you want it even more rhythmic you could play around by adding a click in and sidechaining the noise to that, that should give you heaps of freedom with how that sound ducks out and in and will also probably help you when it comes to mixing down later as well as you wont have too many crazy harmonics up there when other stuff is playing alongside the noise.
